entries.proposition: The trial was double-blind placebo-controlled, with randomisation 1:1, adjunctive to existing antiseizure medicines, over 17 weeks.
entries.snippet: Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either ganaxolone or placebo, as adjunctive therapy to their existing antiseizure medications, which was administered 3 times daily over a 17-week period.

entries.proposition: The sample size was set on the seizure primary outcome only.
entries.snippet: A sample size of 100 patients (50 per group) was required to give 92 % power at a onesided α of 0•025 to detect a between-group difference of 30 % in the percentage change in 28-day major motor seizure frequency

entries.proposition: Non-seizure outcomes were measured by proxy- or parent-reported questionnaires (ADAMS, sleep habits, quality of life), not by a clinician-administered developmental instrument.
entries.snippet: Behaviour was measured using the Anxiety, Depression and Mood Scale (ADAMS), developed as a proxy-report measure to screen mental health in individuals with intellectual disability

entries.proposition: Developmental skills were a baseline covariate from a study-modified 15-item score taken from routine clinical exams, not an outcome.
entries.snippet: For the Modified CDKL5 Development Score, data were collected during routine clinical exams and one point was allocated per item giving a maximum possible score of 15.

entries.proposition: Missing post-treatment data were handled by full-information maximum likelihood; groups were analysed as randomised.
entries.snippet: The effects of ganaxolone on post treatment scores for behaviour, sleep and QOL were assessed with Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) in their original assigned groups

entries.proposition: Two ADAMS subscales were significant at p 0.025 and 0.046; the upper interval bound of the second sits at the line of no effect.
entries.snippet: Effects were statistically significant for the Manic/Hyperactive subscale (effect size = −1.27, 95 % Confidence Interval (CI) −2.38 to −0.16, p = 0.025) and for the Compulsive Behavior subscale (effect size = −0.58, 95%CI −1.14 to −0.01, p = 0.046)

entries.proposition: Depressed Mood moved in the unfavourable direction, not significantly.
entries.snippet: Depressed Mood scores were increased but not significantly (effect size = 0.82, 95%CI −0.22 to 1.86, p = 0.122)

entries.proposition: The total quality-of-life score was higher in the active arm but not significantly.
entries.snippet: The post treatment total QI-Disability score was 2.64 (95%CI −1.74, 7.02) points higher in the ganaxolone group.

entries.proposition: The authors state the upper confidence limits for both significant behaviour effects are close to the line of no effect.
entries.snippet: although the effect sizes were between small and medium and the upper CI values for both domains were close to the line of no effect.

entries.proposition: The sample was sized for seizures and may be inadequate for behaviour and quality of life; the clinically meaningful difference is unknown.
entries.snippet: The sample size was calculated to evaluate a 30 % reduction in the primary seizure outcome, but this sample size may be inadequate to detect meaningful differences in non-seizure outcomes such as behaviour and QOL.

entries.proposition: The authors do not know which differences are clinically meaningful.
entries.snippet: Further, we do not know what differences in the outcomes are clinically meaningful for patients and their families.

entries.proposition: The authors note quality of life may need longer than 17 weeks.
entries.snippet: It is feasible that it takes longer than 17 weeks to observe differences in QOL and that ongoing surveillance of ganaxolone could indicate different effects.

entries.proposition: The seizure-behaviour link was explored only by within-arm correlation because mediation analysis was underpowered.
entries.snippet: The sample size was too small for mediation analyses to explore linkages between ganaxolone use and effects on seizures and non-seizure outcomes

entries.proposition: Raw mean ADAMS manic/hyperactive scores fell in both arms: 7.0 to 4.8 on ganaxolone and 6.3 to 5.2 on placebo.
entries.snippet: Manic/Hyperactive (/15)a N = 89 | 4.8 (3.8) | 5.2 (4.1)
entries.anchor: Table 1, post-treatment ADAMS rows (baseline 7.0 and 6.3 in the rows above)

entries.proposition: Baseline development score was imbalanced between arms (median 2 against 4).
entries.snippet: Median (IQR) Baseline Development Score (/15)a N = 100 | 2 (1–5) | 4 (1–7)

entries.proposition: Daytime sleepiness data were available for 78 children only.
entries.snippet: Mean (SD) Post-treatment Daytime Sleepiness subscale score (/24)a N = 78 | 12.6 (2.7) | 12.2 (3.6)

entries.proposition: Correlation of seizure change with compulsive behaviour has opposite signs in the two arms.
entries.snippet: Compulsive Behaviour | 0.33 (p = 0.04) | −0.35 (p = 0.02)
